full_judgment:
Md. Nuruzzaman J. This Jail Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 29.01.2017 passed by the High Court Division in Death Reference No.07 of 2012 with Jail Appeal No.44 of 2012, accepting the death reference and dismissing the Jail Appeal No.44 of 2012 and thereby affirming the judgment and order of conviction and sentence passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Comilla, convicting the accused under section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860 and sentencing him to death in Sessions Case No.482 of 2011, corresponding to G.R. No.219/2010, arising out of Debidwar P.S. Case No.9 dated 15.11.2010. 

 3. The police, completing the investigation, submitted Charge-sheet No.36 dated 16.03.2011 under section 302/201 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the accused person. 

 5. The learned Sessions Judge framed the charge against the sole accused under section 302/201 of the Penal Code, 1860. The said charge was read over and explained to the accused to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried in accordance with law. 

 9. After conclusion of trial, the learned Sessions Judge, Comilla upon considering the evidence and other materials on record by its judgment and order dated 31.01.2012 convicted the accused Md. Al-Amin under section 302 of the Penal Code, 1860 and sentenced him to death. In other word it was ordered that the accused Md. Al-Amin be hanged by the neck till he is dead. 

 13. Mrs. Shirin Afroz, the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the prosecution in a wretched manner has failed to prove the charge leveled against the accused. Moreover, there is no eye witness to connect the condemned appellant with the alleged murder. Inasmuch as, the circumstantial evidences appearing in the instant case are insignificant and sleazy in nature. So, relying on such evidences, the condemned appellant cannot be held liable for guilty, as well as be given capital punishment. She further submits that the condemned appellant did not make confessional statement voluntarily and the same was obtained from him by the police upon torture and under duress and therefore, no reliance can be placed upon it. According to her, in such a backdrop without independent and substantive evidence, the condemned appellant is liable to be acquitted from the charge leveled against him. She finally submits that the condemned appellant has been languishing in the death cell through the pangs and agony of death sentence for the last 9(nine) years, so, if the conviction of the accused is maintained in that event his sentence may be commuted to one of life imprisonment in view of the fact that the fate of the case mainly hinges on the confessional statement of the accused. In support of his submission, she placed reliance on the case of State Vs. Tohurul Islam and others, reported in 66 DLR 386.
